newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Kelanamas to boost finance exposure.
newsitem.headline: Kelanamas to boost finance exposure.

text.p: Malaysia's Kelanamas Industries Bhd said on Monday it intends to increase its exposure to the finance industry by strategies including pumping additional working capital into its stockbroking arm.

Directors of the property and finance concern said this at a news briefing after the company's extraordinary general meeting on Monday. At the meeting, shareholders approved the sale of a 22 percent stake in shipbuilder Perusahaan Sadur Timah (M) Bhd (Perstima).

Kelanamas said that it realised a capital gain of 113.43 million ringgit from its divestment of the Perstima stake. Malaysian businessman Amin Shah, who already controls Perstima, is the acquiror of the stake.
The divestment of Perstima shares would result in Kelanamas' stake falling from 26 percent to four percent, the company said.
"A substantial portion of the capital gain will be used for additional working capital for Alor Star Securities," said Sallehuddin Kassim, chairman of Kelanamas.
Sallehuddin said 51 percent-owned Alor Star Securities contributes 30 percent of group earnings, which he expects to increase to range of 55 percent to 60 percent over the next two years.
For the 15 months ended December 31, 1995, Kelanamas posted a net loss of 14.33 million ringgit. The 15-month period reflects the change of the company's year-end from September 30 to December 31.
In the 12 months ended September 30, 1994, Kelanamas had a net loss of 1.44 million ringgit.
Sallehuddin also told reporters that the company is in negotiations to acquire a stockbroking company in the Philippines and in Indonesia. He declined to give further details.
He said that other financial services the company would be looking at would include banking, finance and mezzanine finance.
When asked if the company was actively looking for a bank to acquire, Sallehuddin said, "If we can identify one, why not?"
